extracted.intended_audience: authors (especially indie/self-published) looking to promote books on TikTok/BookTok
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for authors on creating, posting, and promoting book-related short videos on TikTok’s BookTok community to grow followers and sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Download and sign up for TikTok
rubrics_metrics.description: Get the TikTok app from Google Play or Apple App Store and sign up using phone, email, or other accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic prerequisite step to have a presence even if you decide not to actively promote; necessary so others can tag you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set up your profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete profile picture, video profile picture, name (add something relevant like 'author'), username (include 'author' or your genre), pronouns, bio, and nonprofit field; connect Instagram or YouTube if you wish to repurpose content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profile settings help filter the algorithm to connect with a target audience; do not skip this step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create your first video (introduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a brief introduction video of yourself as your first post—keep it short and focus on getting content out rather than perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jason Hamilton: 'Try to keep it short, but don't worry too much about the quality. Just get something out there so you can experiment using the tools.' Use available TikTok technical guides if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for 1,000 followers
rubrics_metrics.description: Target an early milestone of 1,000 followers because it unlocks the ability to post a link in your bio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once unlocked you can link to your author website, bookstore link, Goodreads, etc. Example: Jason Hamilton hit 1,000 followers in two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be consistent (posting frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post regularly—when starting, aim for two to four videos a day to maximize visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikTok is a numbers game; frequent posts (15 seconds to 1 minute each) increase chances of being seen. Consistency was credited with follower/sales growth for cited authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment and play with tools
rubrics_metrics.description: You don’t need video skills—use your smartphone and TikTok’s creative tools to experiment with formats and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use face-on-inanimate-object filters if you don’t want to show your face; film flipping a book; try simple or complex edits. Iteration helps find what works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a clear hook (be catchy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open videos with a clear hook—don’t meander; use the first few seconds to get straight to the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter videos typically perform better. Longer videos over a minute are possible but shorter usually get more traction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow other authors and learn from them
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow authors in your genre to learn BookTok culture and watch their most popular videos for inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save sounds from other videos that you like and reuse them; study examples like Ayana Gray, A. L. Knorr, Ann Patchett, Jennifer Millikin, and chloegong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow trends and adapt them bookishly
rubrics_metrics.description: Use trending sounds, effects, and hashtag trends—then create a bookish version to reach users beyond #BookTok followers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following broader TikTok trends can diversify and expand your audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with others (community interaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively like, comment, and follow other BookTok videos—especially those in your genre—to improve the algorithmic recommendations for your feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement helps the algorithm surface relevant videos and connects you to the BookTok community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Stitch (#StitchThis) strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Stitch clips from other creators and record your reaction or response to engage and join conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors use stitching to answer reader questions or share opinions on other BookTok books—add hashtag #stitchthis when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try Duets sparingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Record real-time reaction videos alongside other creators’ clips to create engaging moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less common than stitching but can produce 'golden video moments'—use when it fits the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use hashtags wisely (include #BookTok)
rubrics_metrics.description: Always include #BookTok and add two to four additional relevant hashtags; avoid using too many hashtags (stay under five).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hashtags improve discoverability; look for niche/genre tags like #genretok or #thrillertok. Using too many hashtags can reduce algorithmic pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be genuine and casual
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize authenticity—TikTok favors casual, sincere content over overtly salesy material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casual settings (gym clothes, pajamas) and unscripted moments resonate. Avoid heavy promotional tone, which tends to turn viewers off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the 20/80 rule (promotion vs engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit promotional content to about 20% of your posts and make ~80% of content engaging or community-focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 20% = announcements about new releases or sales; 80% = life-as-author content, stitched clips, reviews, trends, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt BookTok cultural signifiers (crowns, bookshelves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in community visual/cultural cues like using a 'crown' or bookshelves as backdrops to signal BookTok membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cultural icons emerged organically and can help signal belonging; use playful elements (crowns) and bookshelves as consistent visual branding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bookshelves as backdrops/props
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bookshelves to visually cue that you are part of BookTok—animate them or use them as a set when you don’t want to be on camera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shelf backdrops are a recognizable BookTok aesthetic that signals your niche to viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share book reviews and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Post reviews and recommendations for books—this is central to BookTok and can build authority and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some creators adopt a controversial persona in reviews; reviews can cover bestsellers to niche works and help you connect with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use emotional/high-impact moments
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos with high emotion (e.g., showing yourself crying while reading) tend to perform well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-emotion content often increases engagement and shareability; you don't have to be extreme—just authentic emotional reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try platform-specific features (e.g., Penguin Random House link)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use new BookTok features such as the Penguin Random House linking option to tie books to your videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable (e.g., you have a PRH-published favorite), link the book to your video to participate in platform features and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review analytics and iterate
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly check TikTok analytics to identify where followers come from, which hashtags or videos perform best, and refine your strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytics to spot patterns: do more of what works and less of what doesn’t. Track follower sources and tag performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study BookTok examples from successful authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch and learn from concrete BookTok accounts (Ayana Gray, A. L. Knorr, Ann Patchett, Jennifer Millikin, chloegong) to see varied successful approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include vlog-style launch journeys, teaser teasers, 'New to You' recommendation series, tip-sharing for indie authors, meme engagement, ARCs and fanart showcases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious with TikTok-originated publishing offers
rubrics_metrics.description: If TikTok/ByteDance or publishers approach you with contracts or publishing offers, review them carefully and consult a literary agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports indicate offers may resemble traditional publishing contracts but with potentially lower royalties; some industry voices warn about less favorable terms and exclusivity concerns.
